$comment: GENERATED by scripts/build-manifest.mjs — machine-readable context for AI agents and tools. Do not edit.
name: ayywi
description: Lightweight, framework-agnostic, AI-first design system. One CSS class contract for HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, server templates — plus typed React components.

entrypoints.ayywi/css: Full stylesheet (tokens + base + all components) in cascade layers ayywi.tokens < ayywi.base < ayywi.components < ayywi.brand — any unlayered app CSS wins. ayywi/ayywi.min.css is the minified file.
entrypoints.ayywi/ayywi.unlayered.css: Same without cascade layers. Use it when an unlayered CSS reset (Tailwind v3 preflight, normalize.css) would otherwise override components.
entrypoints.ayywi/css/<file>.css: Per-file layered CSS: tokens.css, base.css, then one file per component (button.css, card.css…).
entrypoints.ayywi/fonts.css: Self-hosted brand fonts (Sora, Unbounded, Caveat; woff2, unicode-range subsets). ayywi/fonts-google.css loads them from Google instead.
entrypoints.ayywi: Framework-free JS: tokens, class helpers (buttonClass…), controllers (connectPopover, connectMenu, enhanceTooltip), toast(), setTheme/setDensity/setBrand, cssVar(). Server-safe.
entrypoints.ayywi/react: React components (re-exports everything from ayywi). Marked "use client".
entrypoints.ayywi/elements: Custom elements for any framework or plain HTML: <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-tooltip>, plus the card spotlight. dist/elements.global.js registers them from a <script> and exposes window.ayywi (toast, setTheme, setDensity, setBrand).
entrypoints.ayywi/tokens.json: DTCG-style token source ($value = dark, extensions hold light/density).
entrypoints.ayywi/tokens/<file>: Exports for other platforms: dark.json, light.json, density/*.json (plain DTCG, for Style Dictionary / Figma), ayywi.scss, Ayywi.swift (SwiftUI), Ayywi.kt (Jetpack Compose).
entrypoints.npx ayywi: CLI: `lint` (checks app code against this manifest), `init` (sets up AI agent files + MCP), `mcp` (MCP server over stdio).

conventions.naming: BEM: .ayy-block, .ayy-block__element, .ayy-block--modifier. Modifiers combine: class="ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--sm".
conventions.state: State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, :checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, [open], :popover-open) so every framework drives it the same way.
conventions.theming: No attribute = follow OS. data-theme="dark" | "light" (or class .dark/.light) forces a theme on any element and its subtree.
conventions.density: Controls default to compact (touch on touch-first devices). data-density="compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" on any element resizes buttons, inputs, tabs, switches, checkboxes and menu items below it.
conventions.brands: Semantic tokens can be overridden per brand: load ayywi/brands/<name>.css and set data-brand. Components never change.
conventions.direction: All layout uses logical properties; set dir="rtl" on any ancestor and components mirror.
conventions.elements: Custom elements are light DOM (no shadow root): write the same ayy- markup inside them; they add behaviour. Vue: compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (t) => t.startsWith("ayy-"); Angular: CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA.
conventions.highContrast: Every stateful component has a forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) style using system colours.

rules: Use existing ayywi classes/components and their variants before writing any custom CSS. Never add a second UI kit.
Never hardcode colours (hex, rgb, hsl, named). Use var(--ayy-color-*) tokens; for tints use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ayy-color-text) N%, transparent) or the wash/line tokens.
Use logical properties only: margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end, text-align: start. Never left/right/margin-left/padding-right, so RTL works.

Spacing, radius, font size, shadows and motion come from tokens (--ayy-space-*, --ayy-radius-*, --ayy-text-*, --ayy-control-*, --ayy-shadow-*, --ayy-ease-*, --ayy-duration-*). Control sizes follow data-density — don't hardcode heights.

Theme with data-theme="light|dark" (or nothing = follow OS). Never write separate dark-mode colours; tokens already switch. Rebrand by overriding semantic tokens or loading a brand file, not by restyling components.

Every interactive element keeps its visible :focus-visible ring. Icon-only buttons need aria-label. Form controls need a label. State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, open).
Stateful styles need a @media (forced-colors: active) fallback (Windows High Contrast erases fills).

Prefer animating transform and opacity (use a logical property like inset-inline-start only when the motion must follow text direction). Everything must still work under prefers-reduced-motion — base.css collapses ayy animations.
No :dir() selectors — minifiers rewrite them into :lang() lists that ignore dir="rtl". Logical properties make direction checks unnecessary.
Body text must fall back to system fonts — never remove the system-ui stack from --ayy-font-body (CJK/Arabic/Cyrillic rely on it).

In React import from "ayywi/react"; in other frameworks and plain HTML use the class names, the class helpers from "ayywi" (buttonClass…) and the custom elements from "ayywi/elements" (<ayy-tabs>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>).
Run `npx ayywi lint` after UI changes and fix every error it reports.

attributes.data-theme: "dark" | "light" — force a theme on this element and its subtree. None = follow the OS.
attributes.data-density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" — control sizes for this subtree. None = compact, or touch on touch-first devices.

publicCustomProperties.--ayy-spot: Card spotlight colour (any colour, usually an --ayy-accent-* token).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-mx: Card spotlight pointer X in px (set by React Card or ayywi/elements).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-my: Card spotlight pointer Y in px (set by React Card or ayywi/elements).

utilities.ayy-scroll: Thin, quiet scrollbars on a scroll container.

components.name: Button
components.description: Triggers an action. Pill-shaped, monochrome primary with a subtle lift on hover.
whenToUse: Any action the user can take: submit, open, save, delete.
Links that should look like actions (apply buttonClass() to the <a>).
whenNotToUse: Navigation inside running text — use a plain link.
Toggling a setting on/off — use Switch.

classes.ayy-button: Root. Alone it is the primary button.
classes.ayy-button--secondary: Quiet filled button for secondary actions.
classes.ayy-button--outline: Bordered, transparent. Neutral alternative to secondary.
classes.ayy-button--ghost: No border or fill until hover. Toolbars, icon buttons.

components.js: buttonClass({ variant?, size?, className? }) → string
a11y: Icon-only buttons need aria-label.
Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both).
Visible focus ring on :focus-visible is built in — never remove it.
do: One primary button per view or section; everything else secondary/outline/ghost.
Put the icon before the label; it inherits size from the button (1.25em).
dont: Don't restyle colours per button — add a variant to the design system instead.
Don't use destructive for non-destructive emphasis.

components.name: Card
components.description: Surface that groups related content. Flat at rest with an inset top highlight; optional lift and pointer-following spotlight.
whenToUse: Grouping a unit of content: a project, a person, a plan, a stat.
Clickable tiles in a grid (add interactive).
whenNotToUse: Page sections — use plain layout, not a card around everything.
Nesting cards inside cards.

classes.ayy-card--interactive: Lifts on hover. Use when the whole card is clickable.
classes.ayy-card--spotlight: Pointer-following glow + lit border. Colour via the --ayy-spot custom property.
classes.ayy-card__title: Heading. Use an h2–h4 that fits your outline.
classes.ayy-card__footer: Actions row, pinned to the bottom.

props.spotlight: boolean — tracks the pointer for you

dont: Don't set background colours on cards; the surface token keeps both themes correct.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Small pill label for status, category or count. Optional pulsing status dot.
whenToUse: Status of an item (Synced, Error, Beta).
Category or tag next to a title.
Live indicators (dot).
whenNotToUse: Anything clickable — use Button (ghost/outline, sm).
Long text — badges never wrap.

a11y: Colour is never the only signal — the label text must say the status.
The dot is aria-hidden; it's decorative.
do: Keep labels to one or two words.
Use the status variants for status, accent spotlights for categories.
dont: Don't stack more than three badges in a row.
Don't put buttons inside badges.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Round (or square) picture of a person or workspace, with initials that show when there's no image or it fails to load.
whenToUse: People and workspaces in lists, headers, comments.
Stacks of collaborators (AvatarGroup).
whenNotToUse: Decorative illustrations — use a plain .

classes.ayy-avatar__image: The . Covers the initials when it loads.

components.name: Input
components.description: Single-line text field. Works for every native input type (text, email, search, number, file…).
whenToUse: Short free-text entry: names, URLs, search, API keys.
whenNotToUse: Multi-line text — use Textarea.
On/off — use Switch.

do: Match the input size to neighbouring buttons in a toolbar (sm with sm).
dont: Don't use placeholder as the label.
Don't hardcode widths in px inside flexible layouts — the input fills its container.

components.name: Field
components.description: Form field wrapper: Label + control + hint or error, stacked with consistent spacing.
whenToUse: Every labelled form control: Input, Textarea, Switch, native <select>.
whenNotToUse: Search boxes in toolbars — an aria-label on the Input is enough.

classes.ayy-field--inline: Label and control side by side (Switch, checkbox).
classes.ayy-label: The <label>. Usable on its own too.
classes.ayy-field__hint: Muted helper text under the control.

react.import: import { Field, Label, FieldHint, FieldError } from "ayywi/react";

a11y: Label htmlFor/for must match the control id.
Link hint/error to the control with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" on the control when there's an error.
The label dims automatically when the control inside the field is disabled.
do: Keep hints to one short sentence.
Show errors after the user leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke.
dont: Don't show a hint and an error at the same time — the error replaces the hint.

components.name: Switch
components.description: On/off toggle for a setting that applies immediately. A native checkbox with role="switch".
whenToUse: Settings that take effect instantly (enable sync, dark mode).
whenNotToUse: Choices submitted later with a form's Save button — a checkbox reads better there.
Choosing between more than two options — use Tabs or a select.

classes.ayy-switch: On <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> (preferred) or <button role="switch" aria-checked>. Thumb is ::before.

components.js: switchClass constant

props.checked / defaultChecked: Controlled / uncontrolled, same as a checkbox.
props....rest: All native <input> attributes (name, value, disabled, required…).

a11y: Always pair with a <label for> (Field inline) or aria-label.
Space toggles it; that's native checkbox behaviour.
The thumb direction flips automatically in RTL.
do: Label describes the 'on' state: 'Sync on save', not 'Toggle sync'.
dont: Don't require a Save click after flipping a switch.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Modal dialog built on the native <dialog> element: top layer, inert background, focus handling and Esc for free.
whenToUse: Confirming a destructive action.
Short focused tasks that must finish before continuing (rename, create).
whenNotToUse: Long forms or multi-step flows — use a page.
Non-blocking messages — use an inline notice.

classes.ayy-dialog__title: Heading (h2). Reference it with aria-labelledby on the dialog.
classes.ayy-dialog__footer: Actions. Stacked on mobile, right-aligned (end-aligned in RTL) from 640px.

props.closeLabel: string — accessible name of the close button (translate it). Default "Close"

a11y: Always include a DialogTitle (or aria-label on the dialog).
Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close (native behaviour).
Esc closes; background is inert while open; page scroll is locked.
Opening and closing fade/scale; the closing animation is skipped in browsers without @starting-style and under reduced motion.

Use destructive variant for the confirm button of irreversible actions.
dont: Don't open a dialog from inside another dialog.
Don't render DialogContent's children while closed — the React component already skips them for you.

components.name: Popover
components.description: Non-modal floating panel anchored to a button. Built on the native popover attribute: top layer, click-outside and Esc to close.
whenToUse: Small forms or details next to their trigger (share link, filters, quick edit).
whenNotToUse: A list of actions — use Dropdown menu.
Anything that must block the page — use Dialog.
Hints on hover — use Tooltip.

classes.ayy-popover: On the element with the popover attribute. Surface, padding, shadow, fade/scale transition.

components.js: popoverClass constant; connectPopover(trigger, content, { side?, align?, offset?, onToggle? }) → { open, close, isOpen, update, destroy }

element.children: A trigger <button> (optionally data-ayy-trigger) and an element with the popover attribute.

a11y: Give the content an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at its heading).
The trigger gets aria-expanded automatically; Esc and click-outside close it and focus returns to the trigger.
It's not a focus trap — use Dialog when the user must finish something first.
do: Keep content short; if it scrolls, it probably wants to be a Dialog or a page.
dont: Don't open popovers on hover.
Don't nest popovers more than one level.

components.name: Dropdown menu

whenToUse: Secondary actions for an item (rename, duplicate, delete).
Overflow “⋯” menus in toolbars and table rows.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a value in a form — use Select or Radio.
Navigation between pages — use links.
Rich content or form fields — use Popover.

classes.ayy-menu__shortcut: Keyboard shortcut hint at the end of an item.

events.ayy-select: { value: string, item: HTMLElement } — value is the item's data-value, else its text

element.children: A trigger <button> and a [popover] element with role="menu" containing .ayy-menu__item buttons.

a11y: Opening moves focus to the first item; arrows move, Home/End jump, letters jump to matching items.
Esc or Tab closes the menu and focus returns to the trigger.
Icon-only triggers (⋯) need aria-label.

Keep item labels to a verb + noun: "Rename project".
dont: Don't put form fields or links to other pages in a menu.
Don't nest menus.

import {

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Short hint on hover or keyboard focus. Works with CSS alone; with React Tooltip or <ayy-tooltip> it moves to the top layer (never clipped) and flips at screen edges.
whenToUse: Naming icon-only buttons visually (they still need aria-label).
Short clarifications: shortcuts, truncated values.
whenNotToUse: Essential information — tooltips are invisible on touch devices.
Interactive content (links, buttons) — use a popover or dialog.
CSS-only (no JS) inside overflow:hidden containers — it can be clipped there; use the React component or <ayy-tooltip>.

classes.ayy-tooltip: Wrapper around the trigger. Shows the content on :hover and :focus-within.
classes.ayy-tooltip__content: The bubble (role="tooltip"). Placement via data-side="top|bottom|start|end" (start/end follow text direction).

components.js: tooltipClass, tooltipContentClass constants; enhanceTooltip(host) moves the bubble to the top layer and adds Esc (returns cleanup).

element.children: One focusable trigger and a .ayy-tooltip__content bubble. Ids and aria-describedby are wired for you.

props.children: One focusable element; aria-describedby is added for you

a11y: Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too.
aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically).
Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.
do: Keep it under ~60 characters.
Use side="start"/"end", not left/right, so RTL works.
dont: Don't put the only copy of important info in a tooltip.
Don't wrap disabled buttons — they can't receive focus or hover events reliably.

components.name: Toast
components.description: Short, temporary notification. One framework-free toast() function renders into a shared region in the top layer (visible above dialogs). Pauses while hovered or focused.
whenToUse: Confirming something happened (Saved, Deployed, Copied).
Background results that don't need a decision, optionally with one Undo-style action.
whenNotToUse: Errors the user must fix — show them inline next to the problem.
Anything needing a decision — use Dialog.
Long or important content — it disappears.

classes.ayy-toaster: The shared region toast() creates (aria-live). Position via data-position.

components.js: toast(message, { description?, variant?, duration?, action?: { label, onClick }, id? }) → { id, dismiss }; toast.success/warning/error/info(message, options); toast.dismiss(id?); configureToaster({ position?, label?, closeLabel? }); toastClass({ variant? })
a11y: The region is aria-live="polite"; destructive toasts use role="alert".
Timers pause while a toast is hovered or focused, so there's time to read it and reach its action.
Messages are set with textContent — never HTML.
do: Say what happened in 2–5 words: "Project deleted".
Offer Undo instead of a confirmation dialog for reversible actions.
dont: Don't stack several toasts for one action — reuse an id to update it.
Don't put links the user must follow in a toast.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline message box with optional icon, title, description and actions.
whenToUse: Page- or section-level messages that stay until resolved (billing issue, read-only mode, maintenance).
whenNotToUse: Confirmations that can disappear — use Toast.
Field errors — use FieldError next to the field.
components.js: alertClass({ variant?, className? }) → string; alertTitleClass, alertDescriptionClass, alertActionsClass constants

react.import: import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, AlertActions } from "ayywi/react";

a11y: Static alerts need no role. If it appears in response to an action, add role="alert" (urgent) or role="status" (polite).
The icon is decorative: aria-hidden="true". The text must carry the meaning.
do: Lead with what happened, then what to do about it.
dont: Don't stack several alerts — combine them.
Don't use destructive for things that aren't errors.

components.name: Progress
components.description: Thin progress bar. Determinate (--ayy-value 0–100) or indeterminate.
whenToUse: Sync, upload, install — anything with measurable progress.
Indeterminate: work of unknown length that takes more than ~1s.
whenNotToUse: Quotas or meters that aren't 'progress' — still fine visually, but use role="meter" instead of progressbar.
components.js: progressClass({ tone?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string
a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them).
Give it an accessible name: aria-label or aria-labelledby.
do: Show the percentage or step as text nearby for anything longer than a few seconds.
dont: Don't animate a determinate bar backwards.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Placeholder shapes shown while content loads, with a subtle shimmer.
whenToUse: Content that takes more than ~300ms and has a predictable layout (cards, lists, profile headers).
whenNotToUse: Unknown layouts or long jobs — use Progress.
Instant loads — skeletons that flash are worse than nothing.

classes.ayy-skeleton: Block placeholder. Set its size to match the content.

components.js: skeletonClass({ shape?, className? }) → string
a11y: Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored.
The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Match the real layout closely so nothing jumps when content arrives.
dont: Don't show skeletons for errors or empty states.
